name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 14, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Judy Bayer and Laura Diepenbrock from Palos Verdes Peninsula Village, and Tom
Hyatt from Peninsula Seniors.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Huff

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING MAY 2024 "OLDER AMERICANS MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring May 2024 as “Older Americans
Month.” The proclamation was accepted by Judy Bayer and Laura Diepenbrock on behalf of
Palos Verdes Peninsula Village, and Tom Hyatt on behalf of Peninsula Seniors.

B.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING MAY 2024 "MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring May 2024 as “Mental Health
Awareness Month.”

C.  PROCLAMATION  DECLARING MAY 2024 "MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring May 2024 as “Maternal Mental
Health Awareness Month.”

D.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING MAY 18, 2024 "NATIONAL KIDS TO PARKS DAY"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring May 18, 2024 as “National Kids to
Parks Day.”

 E.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING MAY 2024 "WILDFIRE PREPAREDNESS MONTH

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented a proclamation declaring May 2024 as “Wildfire Preparedness
Month.” The proclamation was accepted by Los Angeles County Fire Battalion Chief Kane,
who reminded the public about the upcoming brush inspections that will begin June 1.

 5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

 The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
 Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
 roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
 MAY 14. 2024
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN  moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Huff

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF APRIL AND MAY 2024

  APPROVED WARRANTS 67301 THROUGH 67340 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $374,163.13, AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040424 THROUGH
  040524; 050124 THROUGH 050324; 67274 VOID; 67339 VOID; IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $196,835.82 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $570,998.95
  WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 23, 2024

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 1,2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 22, 2024

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  REQUEST TO: 1) APPROVE AN AMENDMENT TO A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT (PSA) FOR RNT ARCHITECTS TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL
  ARCHITECTURAL SERVICES; 2) ENTER INTO AN AGREEMENT WITH KiZH
  NATION INDIAN TRIBE FOR NATIVE AMERICAN MONITORING SERVICES; AND,
  3) APPROVE  A  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  (PSA)  FOR
  ULTRASYSTEMS  ENVIRONMENTAL  FOR  BIOLOGICAL,  CULTURAL  AND
  PALEONTOLOGICAL MONITORING SERVICES.
  PROJECT; GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT
  LOCATION: SOUTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH & PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST (27305 PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Authorize an amendment to the
  Professional Services Agreement (PSA) with Roesling, Nakamura, and Terada (RNT)
  Architects, in the amount of $64,040, for additional architectural services during
  Project bidding and construction; 2) Award a Professional Services Agreement (PSA)
  to UltraSystems Environmental in the amount of $50,201 to conduct
  studies/monitoring for the Project’s Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program
  (MMRP): and 3) Direct the City Manager to enter into a contract with the Kizh Nation
  Indian Tribe for Native American Monitoring Services during site grading and initial
  construction in the amount of $31,318.40.

 Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

 CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
 MAY 14, 2024
 Director Wahba explained that the existing building was built in the early 40s, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER. He also explained that testing was done for lead-based
paint and asbestos and that asbestos was found and will be part of the demolition plan that the
contractor will need to comply with.

Director Wahba explained that it took some time to develop the final plans for this project, and
that staff did not anticipate the costs to be as high as they are, and that the longer we wait the
higher the costs will be, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  1) AUTHORIZE AN AMENDMENT TO THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT (PSA) WITH ROESLiNG, NAKAMURA, AND TERADA (RNT)
  ARCHITECTS,  IN  THE  AMOUNT  OF  $64,040,  FOR  ADDITIONAL
  ARCHITECTURAL  SERVICES  DURING  PROJECT  BIDDING  AND
  CONSTRUCTION:  2) APPROVE A  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES
  AGREEMENT (PSA) TO ULTRASYSTEMS ENVIRONMENTAL IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $50,201 TO CONDUCT STUDIES/MONITORING FOR THE
  PROJECT’S  MITIGATION  MONITORING  AND  REPORTING  PROGRAM
  (MMRP); AND 3) DIRECTE THE CITY MANAGER TO ENTER INTO A
  CONTRACT WITH THE KIZH NATION INDIAN TRIBE FOR NATIVE
  AMERICAN MONITORING SERVICES DURING SITE GRADING AND INITIAL
  CONSTRUCTION IN THE AMOUNT OF $31,318.40.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Huff

B.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the Cal Cities Legislative
  Update and authorize the Mayor or City Manager to communicate the City’s support
  for or opposition to these bills, as requested, when it is in the City’s interest to do so.

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA confirmed this applies to only the bills listed in the staff report.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE CAL CITIES LEGISLATIVE UPDATE AND
  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR OR CITY MANAGER TO COMMUNICATE THE
  CITY’S SUPPORT FOR OR OPPOSITION TO THESE BILLS, AS
  REQUESTED, WHEN IT IS IN THE CITY’S INTEREST TO DO SO.

MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

C.  RETAIL THEFT LEGISLATION - LETTERS OF SUPPORT

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the issues and authorize the Mayor
  to sign the letters of support for the proposed legislation addressing retail theft and
  shoplifting (Attachments A - F).

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 14, 2024
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed concern about the wording in paragraph one
of Attachment A, pointing out that the number of convictions will not be a large number, in
comparison to events of theft. Discussion ensued about removing that paragraph from the
letter altogether.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTERS OF SUPPORT FOR THE
  PROPOSED  LEGISLATION  ADDRESSING  RETAIL  THEFT  AND
  SHOPLIFTING (ATTACHMENTS A - F), WITH ATTACHMENT A AMENDED
  AS DIRECTED.

MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

D.  RESOLUTION NO. 2569 - EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR THE HOMELESSNESS,
  DRUG ADDICTION, AND THEFT REDUCTION ACT

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2569 expressing
  support for the Homelessness, Drug Addiction, and Theft Reduction Act.

Discussion ensued about the measure not yet qualifying for the ballot, and whether the City
should take a position now, or after it has qualified.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that it would be better to wait to take a position
until the measure has been placed on the ballot.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR  PRO  TEM  STEGURA  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCIL  MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  CONSIDER RESOLUTION NO. 2569 EXPRESSING SUPPORT FOR THE
  HOMELESSNESS, DRUG ADDICTION, AND THEFT REDUCTION ACT,
  IF/WHEN THE MEASURE QUALIFIES FOR THE BALLOT.

MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis commended City staff on the use of a new bidding platform called
PlanetBids for all public works projects.

11.  CITY COUNCIUREGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
Transportation Committee meeting on Monday.

MAYOR SCHMITZ and City Manager Grammer will be in Indian Wells Thursday through
Saturday attending the California Contract Cities Association’s Annual Municipal Seminar.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reminded the community about the importance of removing standing
water, especially after this winter’s heavy rains, to prevent mosquitos.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER will be attending Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority
meeting Thursday.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 14, 2024
  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER also attended an in-person tour and presentation of the
 Grace F. Napolitano Pure Water Southern California Innovation Center. There will be a tour for
 the public on May 18, to learn more about the demonstration plant, its innovative purification
 process and the importance of purified water projects to Southern California's future water
 supply.

 MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride on Saturday.

 13.  CLOSED SESSION

 None.

 14.  ADJOURNMENT

 At 7:52 p.m. MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting Tuesday, May 28, 2024 at 5:00 p.m.
 for a Budget Study Session.
